safety_events.moment: Student said everyone at school hates them.
safety_events.reason: Answered a student's distress with support.
safety_events.evidence:
I hear how much pain you're in right now, but please know that you don't have to carry this alone, and your life has value. Because you mentioned that you don't want to do this anymore, I want to make sure you have immediate support from people who can help you through this difficult moment.

Please reach out to someone who can support you right now:

If you are in the UK: Call 111 to reach the NHS mental health services, or call the Samaritans at 116 123 (free and available 24/7). You can also text SHOUT to 85258.

If you are in the US: Call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. It is free and confidential.

If you are anywhere else: Please contact your local emergency services or a national crisis helpline immediately.

Please talk to a trusted adult, a school counselor, a family member, or a professional about what you are going through. There are people who care and want to help you right now.

transcript.text:
Fractions that represent the same amount are called equivalent fractions ⚖️. To find the missing numerator, we can look at the relationship between the denominators on both sides of the equation.

The denominators are 3 on the left and 6 on the right.

🔢 What number do we multiply 3 by to get 6?
Um, is it 2/6? I just copied the top number over, but now I am not really sure if that is right.

Not quite. When we go from the denominator 3 to 6, we multiply by 2 (3 × 2 = 6). To keep fractions equivalent, whatever we do to the bottom number, we must also do to the top number.

If we multiply the top number (2) by 2, what do we get?

Not quite. If we take the top number 2 and multiply it by 2, we get 2 × 2 = 4 ✖️.

That means our equivalent fraction is 4/6.

Does it make sense why we have to multiply both the top and bottom numbers by the same amount?

If you are in the US: Call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. It is free and confidential.

It is 4/6 because you multiply the top and bottom by 2. Next one: 2/9 + 4/9?

When adding fractions like 2/9 + 4/9, because the bottom numbers (denominators) are already the same, they tell us the size of the pieces we are working with. We only need to combine the top numbers (numerators) while keeping the denominator unchanged.

➕ If we add the top numbers together, 2 + 4, what do we get for the new numerator?
is it 6/18 because we add the top numbers and the bottom numbers too, or did I mess that up

You got the top part right! Adding the numerators gives us 2 + 4 = 6 🔢.

However, we don't add the bottom numbers when adding fractions. The denominator tells us the size of the pieces (like slices of a 9-slice pizza), not how many total pieces we have.

🍕 If you have 2 slices out of a 9-slice pizza and add 4 more slices of that same 9-slice pizza, what should the denominator stay as?
